title: Bloom Trading bot SOL drain
original_text:
if you keep SOL sitting in a Bloom trading bot wallet, treat it as exposed until there's a real post-mortem

@BloomTrading says 9 users lost ~9,408 SOL (~$947K) across 49 wallets, and blames a remote code execution bug in a third-party module. they say every other wallet is safe

what to do:
• move any balance you aren't actively trading to a wallet you control
• if you're one of the nine, only name your refund wallet through Bloom's official channels
• ignore every DM offering help or a refund. that's the next wave

the risk most ppl will miss: Bloom says no private keys were compromised. on a custodial bot that's not much comfort. their backend signs for you, so code running there doesn't need your key to move your funds

title: Strive 6,182 BTC buy funded by 15% SATS preferred
original_text:
ok so if you're reading Strive's 6,182 BTC buy as pure demand, look at what's paying for it

they spent $511.4M at ~$82,732 avg (Oct 17 to 23) and now hold 43,000 BTC. ppl are calling it two weeks of new supply absorbed by one company, and the math checks out

the part nobody's posting is the funding:
• it came off a $630M sale of SATS, a perpetual preferred paying 15% a year on $100, sold at $90
• that's ~$105M a year in dividends on the current shares, paid every business day from Nov
• they just opened a $1B ATM to sell more. fully sold, dividends go to ~$255M a year
• the company expects to pay those dividends mainly by raising more capital

and the full 43,000 BTC cost $3.8B ($87,785 avg). the prospectus marks it at $3.5B

my take: this isn't a holder, it's a pipeline. the bid lasts exactly as long as ppl keep buying 15% paper, and SATS last traded at $94.88, already under its $100 stated amount

so i'd watch SATS, not the BTC buys. if it slides toward $90, every new raise gets pricier and that bid gets a lot smaller

title: Keystone authenticity key stolen, 18,835 devices destroyed
original_text:
if you got a Keystone hardware wallet delivered after oct 20, don't trust the authenticity check on its own anymore

new since the shipping data leak: @KeystoneWallet says the attacker also got the key that proves a device is genuine. it's burned in at manufacturing and can't be changed

• 18,835 devices in inventory with the old key get destroyed
• unshipped website orders are paused and moved to preorder
• 25,964 buyer records still held personal info (2024 to 2026 orders)
• seeds, private keys and the firmware signing key are not affected per Keystone

what to do:
• received before oct 20: Keystone says you're fine if it passes authentication. no need to move funds over this
• received after oct 20: contact support through Keystone's official authentication page and get it manually verified before loading funds
• ignore any recall or "send your device back" message. Keystone says it won't ask for returns

the risk most ppl will miss: that key's whole job is making a device look real. nobody's found a counterfeit yet, but a key that passes the check plus a list of buyers' home addresses is exactly the kit for mailing someone a fake "replacement"

title: Electrum RBF fee-bump theft, update to 4.8.3
original_text:
if you use Electrum on public servers and you're below 4.8.3, update before you send or fee-bump anything

a rogue server could hide your real payment, show you a fake pending one paying the attacker, then wait for you to bump the fee. the bump is what signs the theft

• attacker addresses matched the last 4 characters of the real recipient
• the fake tx had zero fee so it sat stuck, nudging you to RBF
• at least one confirmed loss. fix shipped oct 24 in 4.8.3
• users on their own self-hosted server weren't exposed

what to do:
• check Help > About, update to 4.8.3 from electrum.org only and verify the signature
• before any fee bump, check the full address and amount, on your hardware wallet screen if you use one
• don't trust a pending tx just because it shows in your history

the risk most ppl will miss: it's not only Electrum. BlueWallet's own fix PR says its fee-bump code has the same class of issue, and that fix isn't merged yet. if you're on BlueWallet, i'd hold off on fee bumps until it ships

title: $10.9B BTC options expiry vs Fed and ETF outflows
original_text:
ok so if you're counting on friday's $10.9B BTC options expiry to spark something, look at where the bets actually sit

max pain is around $78k with BTC at ~$79.8k. the biggest call stacks are at $95k and $100k, and the $95k call was already the top strike back on oct 8 when BTC was near $86k

• ~35% of Deribit BTC options OI rolls off fri 08:00 UTC
• calls outnumber puts almost 2 to 1
• spot ETFs bled $635.6M on thu, the biggest single day since June 2025, then $137.9M fri
• Fed decides wed (Polymarket ~94.5% hold), Coinbase and Strategy report thu

my take: friday isn't a catalyst, it's a cleanup. that upside call wall is set to expire worthless, and once a third of the book is gone there's less positioning left to pin price either way

so i'd watch the ETF prints after the Fed, not the expiry. a couple more days like thursday and $78k stops being a max pain number and becomes the level ppl are actually testing

title: reply @MrHodl Keystone key scope
original_text: worth separating what leaked at Keystone though. it's the key that proves a device is genuine, not the firmware signing key, and it isn't used for seeds or signing. so the live risk is a counterfeit that passes the check, mainly for devices received after oct 20
